newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official downplays trade impact from dlr/yen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official downplays trade impact from dlr/yen.

text.p: A senior U.S. Commerce Department official on Monday played down the impact of a stronger dollar against the yen on the trade deficit with Japan.

The official, who spoke with reporters on condition of anonymity, said major structural changes in the Japanese economy may mean that the bilateral trade balance is less susceptible to currency fluctuations than it appeared to have been in the past.
"The exchange-rate change may not have as profound an effect as in the past," the official said, but he declined to forecast the direction of the U.S.-Japan trade gap.
The deficit with Japan has been shrinking in recent months but some private economists have said it might resume widening again because of the strength of the dollar.
The dollar rose to a 42-month high against the yen Monday.
